stem: During secondary succession, which of these best describes why decomposing pioneer plants give way to larger, more complex plants species, such as hardwood trees?

options.label: F
options.text: Increased amounts of sunlight are able to reach the ground while the pioneer species are decomposing.

options.label: G
options.text: Increased soil temperatures from decomposing pioneer species help tree seeds germinate more quickly.

options.label: H
options.text: Increased amounts of decomposing pioneer species remove nutrients that tree seedlings need to grow and mature.

options.label: J
options.text: Increased amounts of soil from decomposing pioneer species allow plants with more extensive root systems to become established.
